---
title: "Benchmark and Independent Backends"
subtitle: "Experimental execution, numerical ownership and truthful observations"
---

**Status:** CONVERGING. This is the candidate contract for the authorized
benchmark experiment. The interfaces below describe intended implementation;
they do not claim completed numerical, performance or device observations.
Existing `solve`, `evaluate`, `optimize` and `resolve` keep their Julia contract.
No durable test changes or stabilization are assigned.

## Public boundary

The candidate entrypoint is
`run.benchmark(ref, spec, *, workspace, benchmark=BenchmarkSpec(), parameters=None, progress=None, resume_from=None)`
returning `BenchmarkResult`. Supported operations are complete Direct S/Y/Z,
diagonal roots, scalar response elements and Optimization expressions built
from those quantities. Original, retained and transformed Views are supported.
HB and other quantity families fail explicitly; there is no backend fallback.

`BenchmarkSpec` selects arms, CPU thread profiles, device, complete-task repeats
and an immutable mesh declaration. Defaults are one full task sample for each
CPU arm and thread profile 1/32. This scope supports CPU devices only; GPU
requests fail explicitly. CUDA, ROCm and Apple GPU execution are excluded from
this Goal. All numerical arrays use Float64/Complex128.

`cpu_threads` continues to declare the physical affinity quota and Python host
NumPy/BLAS and JAX/XLA resources. Optional `julia_threads` and
`julia_blas_threads` are positive integer overrides for native Julia only,
across all Julia arms. Each `None` independently resolves to the selected quota;
existing defaults are unchanged. The configured integers/nulls are part of the
canonical benchmark declaration. Each native task binds effective
`julia_threads` and `julia_blas_threads` separately into its configuration,
backend/environment identity, ready validation and checkpoint ownership.
Actual Julia ready telemetry retains its existing `blas_threads` field.
Overrides do not mutate the Plan, ordinary/HB policy, candidate scheduling or
Python/JAX thread resources, and are not capped by a new quota comparison.
The quota32 experiment compares Julia32/BLAS32 with Julia32/BLAS1 under the
same physical inputs and affinity allocation; no performance or default-policy
conclusion is established by this declaration.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P[Immutable Plan and prepared request] --> H[Python benchmark task]
  H --> O[Original Julia whole task]
  H --> C[Python physical compiler and View]
  C --> S[Python continuation and CMA host]
  S --> J[Julia numerical adapter: reuse or pivoted LU]
  S --> X[Independent JAX numerical adapter]
  O --> E[Verified observations and task artifacts]
  J --> E
  X --> E
  E --> R[Read-only JSON and HTML report]
```

Python selects the arm directly. The JAX arm must not invoke Julia for runtime
discovery, preflight, lowering, root evaluation, Optimization or reporting.
The original whole-task arm is separate from both common-host Julia arms.
The base package has no JuliaPkg dependency. Install `scnsim[benchmark]` on
Python 3.12 and select `arms=("python_jax",)` for JAX-only CPU execution.
Julia arms additionally require `scnsim[julia]` and a manually provided Julia
1.12.6 on PATH or `PYTHON_JULIAPKG_EXE`; feature calls never acquire Julia or
fall back to another backend. The default arm declaration remains unchanged.
Existing native compile/explain/compiled-schematic and new ordinary numerical
operations require Julia; authoring, result reading, resolve and verified cache
reuse remain independent of executable discovery.

## Shared descriptor and ownership

`benchmark/models.py` owns the shared immutable data structures and numerical
adapter Protocol; `prepared.py` binds the canonical experimental declaration.
`compiler.py`, `mesh.py` and `views.py` own physical lowering and candidate View
realization. `optimization.py` owns candidate and leaf order, parameter
transforms, continuation, caches and strict-best selection. `api.py` delegates
the public request. `backends/` owns local numerical evaluation and complete
Newton loops. `process.py`, `task.py`, `storage.py`, `timing.py` and `identity.py`
own processes, task state, evidence, observed intervals and runtime identity.
`visualization/benchmark.py` consumes verified observations without solving.

The compiler consumes the existing canonical Plan v2 descriptor, resolved
parameter point and request-owned mesh policy. `CompiledModel` carries ordered
node/Port IDs, real C/K/G(n,n), B(n,p), R(p,p), M(p), and series-RL blocks with
incidence(n,r) and R/L(r,r). Frequency-dependent branch impedance is retained;
it is not flattened into a constant conductance. Evidence includes resolved
bindings, expanded branches and actual per-line grids.

`RealizedView` carries the transformed full physical model, ordered terminal
IDs, active public coordinates, zero-based selected indices, full(n,p)
coordinate-to-Port map and candidate-derived lineage. `original_node_ids`
identifies the map row axis; transformed `model.node_ids` identifies the
operator axis. These axes need not have the same ordering. The selected map has
shape(q,p), Bk(n,q), Rk/Dk(q,q) and Go(p,p). Boundary arrays
are absent for a non-Port-realizable root-only View. Internal nodes stay in the
model. Transform weights derive from each candidate's full capacitance cut;
ordinary transpose, not conjugate transpose, defines physical congruence.
Prepared descriptors retain ordered physical/selected IDs, block shapes and
actual section counts. JAX executables specialize on numerical tensor shapes,
dtypes, job kind, response family, Port realizability and batch size;
coefficients and indices remain runtime arguments, and lineage/node IDs are
not compilation keys. Packing equal RL coefficients can change group shapes
without changing total node count. `new_shape` records first executable-signature
preparation through `.lower(...).compile()`, not proof of an uncached machine-code
build or a changed matrix dimension. One batch's timing is repeated on its
result records; aggregation must count that batch once.

Arrays are detached onto immutable byte buffers. Record payloads are canonical
JSON bytes; accessors return detached documents. Adapters cannot mutate the
Plan, descriptors or another candidate's evidence. Scalar measurement records
use explicit `{"f64": "<big-endian binary64 hex>"}` tags, including observed
non-finite outcomes. Physical parameter envelopes retain their existing
`si_value_f64`/unit/dimensionality schema. Group interval bounds use
`lower_f64`/`upper_f64`; no decimal serialization shifts a boundary.
`record_bytes` is the single observation codec; `record_document` decodes its
tags. Explicit fields ending `_f64` remain exact hexadecimal strings.

## Numerical adapter call

`NumericalBackend.identity() -> dict`,
`evaluate_batch(tuple[EvaluationJob, ...]) -> tuple[EvaluationResult, ...]`,
and `close()` are the common adapter calls. The original whole-task control
does not implement this numerical adapter interface.

Jobs have opaque host IDs and kind `direct`, `diagonal_root` or
`response_element`. Direct jobs carry frequencies in Hz and return S/Y/Z with
axes(frequency,output,input). Scalar responses carry one frequency, family and
zero-based terminal output/input indices. Root jobs carry terminal coordinate
index, root hint in Hz and complex starting omega in rad/s. Adapters perform
the complete local Newton procedure and return root omega, local slope and
certificate evidence. The Python host owns baseline-to-candidate continuation,
including intermediate lowering and View realization.
Standalone `DiagonalRootSpec` tasks evaluate the sealed Plan baseline in the
exact declared View, then publish its actual root as a
`scnsim.benchmark_root_anchor` through the acknowledged `baseline_ready`
checkpoint handoff before any nonbaseline work. Every nonbaseline point starts
from that anchor, using the same dyadic continuation routine as Optimization.
Candidate-dependent Views and actual intermediate observations remain explicit;
requested points retain their order, with actual baseline and duplicate results
reused. This root-anchor record is distinct from a CMA-resumable checkpoint;
standalone tasks do not accept `resume_from`.

Batch outputs preserve exact job order and IDs, including typed numerical
failures (`kind`, `stage`, `detail`, evidence). The host adds candidate/leaf
context and decides existing candidate-failure handling. Direct/root/response
tasks emit actual ordered observations, then raise the first numerical failure
as its existing public SCNSimError type; failed solving cannot claim a successful
terminal. Optimization baseline/fatal failures also raise, while legitimate
candidate failures alone yield infinity. Process death,
corrupt protocol and compiler invariants are fatal; they are not candidate
infinity. Every returned outcome means the actual device/process work has
completed. Adapters may group compatible work but must restore input order.
Diagonal roots retain the scalar Schur/slope certificate, 32-iteration procedure,
bitwise stagnation behavior, analytic derivatives and native failure distinctions.
Excluded root families do not justify an unused generic determinant/cofactor
implementation. This experiment adds no tolerance Gate.

## Host state and task protocol

Common-host Optimization uses optional `cmaes==0.13.1` ask/tell, existing
seed/sigma/population/complete-generation budget and SCNSim transforms with
new algorithm IDs. Bounds are handled by those transforms; library bounds are
None and `should_stop` is not activated. The local RNG mapping is
`signed64-two-uint32-v1`. Tell receives a copy because it sorts its inputs.
No Julia trajectory or replay equivalence is claimed.

The baseline and root anchors are committed before the first ask. Common Python
arms default to generation checkpoints and boundary diagnostics. The declaration
`BenchmarkSpec()` keeps the four existing arms: omitted `diagnostics=None`
resolves to `"boundary"` for common Python arms and the existing `"immediate"`
policy for original whole-Julia. Explicit `diagnostics="immediate"` remains
available. Original whole-Julia rejects explicit `"boundary"` or checkpoint
`"off"` before launch; explicit options are never ignored. The canonical request
records the effective diagnostics map by declared arm; each Python task request
and evidence writer receives its concrete string. The map and selected arm bind
the task identity. Ordinary Julia APIs are unchanged. Checkpoint off disables CMA-resumable
snapshots, including the initial CMA snapshot; required baseline/root anchors,
committed numerical observations and terminal results remain durable.

Generation checkpoints are post-tell/pre-next-ask and retain numeric CMA state,
explicit RNG snapshot, strict-best and baseline references and committed
cache/history links. Root anchors live once in the baseline evidence block;
generation snapshots reference that block rather than copy its anchors. Immutable completed-generation blocks own ordered
candidate occurrences and newly evaluated candidate values; events, checkpoints
and reports reference that authority rather than embedding repeated cache and
history copies. Small commit records publish a generation only after its linked
content is durable. An interruption before HEAD replacement leaves the previous
commit selected. After replacement, storage reconciles the selected HEAD and
whether its durability is confirmed; an uncertain or newly selected delta is not
blindly replayed. Unreferenced files alone are not evidence of a completed
generation. Storage
owns locks, atomic publication, file/directory durability and verification;
optimization owns the numerical cache, order and CMA snapshot. Reopen/resume
verifies the selected links and reconstructs working state. Read-only assembly
produces complete report documents without migrating historical records.

Snapshots bind request, backend, dependency, source, mesh, device and resource
identities. Untold populations are observed but regenerated on exact-identity
resume; no pickle or blind getstate restores authority. Candidate and objective
order remains observable even when numerical jobs are batched. Equal costs
retain the earlier strict-best winner. No cross-source resume is promised.

Immediate diagnostics persist each event. With no public progress callback,
default boundary diagnostics buffer candidate and other diagnostic events until
a generation commit, terminal outcome, or handleable interruption/failure.
Candidate numerical records remain retained at the generation barrier; boundary
buffering does not delete them. A public
callback forces its corresponding event and required references durable before
notification, even in boundary mode. Callback exceptions and KeyboardInterrupt
propagate with their original ownership; persistence/protocol/process errors
remain fatal and never become candidate Inf. A hard kill may lose unflushed
diagnostics; reports identify an unknown/missing tail from the recorded
lifecycle rather than claiming a complete stream or a known lost-event count.
There is no persisted diagnostic-completeness marker. A terminal flush covers
records received by the parent, not unobserved child-side work. Already committed results and checkpoints retain their guarantees.
Normal interruption flushes available evidence without publishing an incomplete
population as a completed generation. Profiling stays outside the measured
store. These persistence guarantees do not themselves imply a measured speedup.
The Human-selected defaults are generation checkpoints and boundary diagnostics
for common Python arms.

For each full population, the host identifies unique effective parameter
records, prepares one physical model per unique candidate and one View per
candidate/declaration, then batches independent numerical jobs across those
candidates in objective/leaf order. Returned results are consumed in original
candidate order. Task-local material caches reuse immutable RLGC matrices,
Cholesky factors and modal delays; length, sections, dx and capacitance-derived
View weights remain candidate data. Dependent continuation steps remain local
to the failed candidate and retain the existing failure distinctions.

`BenchmarkSpec(task_kind="cohort", cohort_bytes=...)` declares a separate ordered
array of canonical `parameter_set_v2` inputs. Partial bindings override the
task's effective baseline closure, with captured identity/type/unit checks.
Optimization-declared extrapolation authority remains unchanged. A cohort
acquires its own baseline anchors and cache, evaluates its ordered candidates
through the same numerical batching path, and emits no CMA ask/tell or
Optimization checkpoint. Input provenance is the authored physical declaration;
prior native output is not an eligibility condition. Full tasks remain the
default; original whole-Julia controls explicitly reject cohort dispatch.

`TaskEvent(task_id, sequence, kind, payload_bytes)` is the storage handoff.
Kinds are ready, authorized, started, timing, baseline_ready,
checkpoint_committed, population_observed,
generation_ready, evaluation, progress, completed, interrupted and failed. Payloads bind
their request/arm/sample identities. Ready events propose immutable content;
only storage's acknowledged evidence commit permits the host to advance;
a CMA checkpoint reference is present only when checkpointing is enabled.
`generation_ready` hands off the new generation block and optional resume snapshot;
`evaluation` includes its ordinal/context and numerical outcome. Interrupt and
callback exceptions keep their existing ownership; partial evidence remains
readable. Public progress receives a frozen `TaskEvent` after its observation
is durable, including native original-Optimization `progress` events. Python
population generations are 1-based; baseline generation is 0. Benchmark
propagates the original callback exception and `KeyboardInterrupt`; the ordinary
`optimize()` callback wrapper remains unchanged. A report-rendering failure cannot overwrite a numerical outcome.

`TaskContext` binds request hash, arm, sample, attempt ID, environment hash,
device and CPU threads. Every child frame carries that context in its payload;
the parent authorizes the ready-frame hash before work. Canonical request files
and bounded canonical frames use no shell or pickle. Shared `array_record` /
`array_from_record` encode dtype(float64/complex128), shape and row-major
little-endian binary64 `data_hex`; zero-based index collections remain JSON
integer lists. An Optimization checkpoint payload has
schema/version, context, generation, next evaluation ordinal, baseline/anchors,
best reference, numeric CMA state, RNG state and committed cache/history links.
Historical full-cache checkpoints remain readable through their original format;
new writes use one current format without in-place migration. Numerical
terminal markers contain counts and selection references; read-only assembly
restores the existing ordered baseline/candidate/point bodies from evidence.
Standalone root continuation rows remain evidence, separate from requested
point rows. Cohort and standalone anchor barriers never create CMA resume
checkpoints. Explicit resume with checkpoint off fails before replay. Storage
verifies staged content, atomically publishes it and returns its exact hash
acknowledgment. Arms run serially to avoid competing resource profiles.

Each independent arm/profile/repeat has a fresh sample workspace and task ID.
The request declaration is shared; sample/runtime evidence is distinct.
Its semantic analysis contains operation, View, Spec and parameter source;
the original analysis hash is a source reference. Common-host transforms have
their own IDs. Original Julia runtime identities are not transplanted onto
JAX tasks or benchmark numerical records, and benchmark observations do not
fabricate existing AnalysisResult identities.
New writes use the benchmark v2 journal: a declaration/task manifest, task/global
HEAD pointers, immutable commit chains and referenced numerical value blocks.
Each mutation reopens its HEAD under the workspace lock, publishes content
before the pointer and releases the lock before callbacks. Historical v1
workspaces remain read-only through their original format. The verified
materializer expands occurrence records and adds Python terminal
`numerical_observations` with exact compact `terminal_summary`, actual value-block
artifact references and the recorded best ordinal. Partial records have no
fabricated terminal artifact or winner. These are source-level candidate
interfaces; installed-wheel recovery and performance evidence remain pending.

`BenchmarkResult` stores a canonical observation manifest. Its JSON document is
detached; the intended `open(workspace)` reconstruction is read-only. HTML
rendering consumes this result and retained partial outcomes without execution.
The manifest binds declaration/source identities and targets, and contains
independent samples with exact Plan/View/Spec/effective inputs, requested and
realized mesh, backend/device/resources/environment/source/dependencies,
process launches and thread/affinity observations. It separates ordered cohort
outcomes from closed-loop generation/checkpoint/winner records, and retains
measurements, actual numerical records, artifact references and report errors.
Target records bind acquisition source/result identity, selector, unit and
value. Only the original Julia arm references actual existing AnalysisResults;
new arms use benchmark-owned records. Original Julia sweep recovery retains
its existing point checkpoint lifecycle; artifact roles
`original_julia_point_checkpoint_record`,
`original_julia_point_checkpoint_attempt` and
`original_julia_point_checkpoint_seal` reference the actual record, source
attempt and seal bytes. `point_checkpoint_count` records the existing published
point count. Native terminal and partial-failure handoffs additionally retain
post hoc numerical observations from the already verified result, baseline
checkpoint and generation ledgers. Records preserve native order and their
actual source artifact references; direct arrays use the shared array codec.
The renderer summarizes those recorded values without inventing per-evaluation
timestamps, task durations, a winner or a terminal result artifact. The
terminal result reference remains null when only partial checkpoint/ledger
observations exist. The existing record codec preserves exact tagged values.
Native parameter sweeps retain the verified point order, requested parameter
sets, statuses and actual point payload/chunk references. Successful Direct
point arrays are materialized once using the existing decoder semantics;
post-stop partial observations share verified checkpoint records and payloads.
Public checkpoint selection remains unchanged. Native point records have no
invented per-point timestamps.
Direct point decoding retains the original producer catalog for manifest
verification and a localized copy only for reading from the point directory.
The stored catalog, manifest bytes, digests and metadata checks remain exact.
If post hoc observation decoding also fails after a native failure, the
original terminal failure remains primary; `numerical_observation_error`
records the secondary diagnostic and the raised error chains its cause.
Reconstruction never binds a workspace,
cleans it, retries a task or chooses the latest success.
Each new measurement carries its invocation clock mapping (`id`, `source`,
`unit`, `monotonic_origin_ns`); `start_ns` is relative to that row's origin.
Historical rows and their recorded root clock binding remain unchanged. A
legacy row without its own clock is labeled as such; the report does not infer
an origin or place distinct invocation clocks on a shared start-time axis.
Durations and inclusive overlap remain explicit rather than summed.

## Mesh experiment and observation contract

Dynamic sections use the current line policy. Full-range fixed counts derive
from maximum 6mm lengths for each Chapter7 line. Grouped fixed counts use
[2,4]mm with left/right maximum4/6mm and (4,6]mm with maximum6/4mm. The request
binds explicit per-line counts, group endpoints/inclusivity, parameter identity
and derivation evidence. Physical length stays x and8mm-x; dx=length/N. The Plan
is unchanged. The chosen strategy applies to all continuation intermediate
points and is recorded with actual compiled grids. No mesh strategy becomes an
automatic model default or a certified error bound.

Required real cases are Chapter2 existing C80–140fF tuning to6.2GHz and its
two-View root/S11 case with Julia targets measured at C120fF/L5.8nH; Chapter7
M40/M80 Direct61-point1–10GHz and position Optimization with a common actual
dynamic-M80 x2mm S21 magnitude target at grid index35; the existing Chapter3
scalar line and Chapter4 transformed6.2GHz response. Group-boundary nextafter
neighbors, common candidate cohorts and full closed-loop CMA are separate
observations. Target quantities and source/result identities are sealed before
comparisons. No synthetic matrices or unmeasured targets stand in for them.

`Measurement` records task/stage, monotonic start/duration, work counts, named
memory observations and details. Record startup, initialization, first JIT,
new-shape compilation, repeated evaluations and synchronized completion within
the same task. Inclusive end-to-end time includes preparation/process/lowering,
optimization/transfers/solve/commit/decode. Trace sealing and HTML rendering are
separate intervals; overlapping stages are not summed. Results retain complex
numbers, roots/linewidths, cache/work/compilation observations, grids, ranking,
winners and refinement/boundary differences without pass/fail thresholds.

Implementation validation remains the work packet's actual installed-wheel
cases, Julia-blocked CPU JAX observations, exact resume/interrupt/
partial-report behavior, inspected HTML, independent reviews and required
existing CI. This contract does not authorize durable test changes or acceptance.
